crime: {WITCH_NAME} was known as the prison's songwriter, but every song she gave the evening circle came from a dead friend's handwritten songbook. Weeks earlier, she had burned it and kept the ash in a tin. Each afternoon, alone in the guest house's water-spirit room, she raised the book, copied out the next song, then released it back to ash. The organizer who had founded the circle around those songs also set its time and place and looked after the room. At breakfast, the organizer announced that starting the next day the whole circle would join {WITCH_NAME} there in the afternoons and watch her write. With a roommate in her cell, that had been {WITCH_NAME}'s only hour alone.

That afternoon, {WITCH_NAME} carried a covered pail and a cleaning cloth past the girls sitting outside the prison entrance and across the grounds to the water-spirit room. Inside, she took up the incinerator ash from the pail and raised the worn matting, bedding, and sweepings that had made it. She did not release the restored material; it remained in place as a low bank across the inside threshold and along both side walls, with the middle clear. At dusk, the organizer came alone to prepare the room. The organizer lit the lamp by the door, crossed to the cushions at the far wall, and stayed there. Outside the room, {WITCH_NAME} waited until the organizer was beside the cushions, then stepped to the doorway, tipped the lamp into the threshold bank, and retreated. The spilling oil set the threshold bank alight; fire ran along both walls and closed the room's only exit before the organizer could return.
The other girls kept the fire from the rest of the guest house, but the room burned to its frame with the organizer inside. At first, the fallen lamp looked accidental.

But the circle had furnished the room with only two cushions, the low table, and the lamp. The deepest burns ran across the threshold and along both walls, where nothing had stood. Loose incinerator ash lay over those marks, with no recognizable charred matting or bedding; everyone knew a restored object returned to its source ash when destroyed again. {WITCH_NAME} claimed the covered pail had held water and the cloth was for wiping the low table and lamp before the evening circle. The girls outside the entrance confirmed that she had carried the pail and cloth to the room that afternoon, and that no other container or bulky load had gone there. The burn pattern required a bank of fuel, and only her power could have made it from the ash hidden in the pail she carried.
fields.epitaph: The cloth kept her shape. Her songs had never contained a note of her own.
execution: A flower press built to a girl's size stood open. Layers of cloth covered the lower iron board, and an upper iron board was joined to it by a screw at each corner. She was laid face down on the cloth and covered with more layers before the upper board was placed over her.

The screws turned a quarter turn at a time, moving from corner to corner. The upper board bore down on her back as the lower board pressed into her chest, and the cloth took the shape of her body. The screws kept turning until her chest no longer rose. The press remained closed.

magic.name: Raised from Ash
magic.text: Ash held in her hands becomes the intact material or object that burned to make it, restored to its former size.
